newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea wet Brent settles after fall, grades firm.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea wet Brent settles after fall, grades firm.

text.p: The North Sea crude market saw little action on Monday, reflecting on a steep fall in Dated Brent values late on Friday.
Wet Brent slipped 17 cents to trade at August parity, and the market was expected to ease even lower. The August 10-12 cargo was sold on a quotes-related basis on Monday.
A U.S. refiner kept an August 12-14 cargo early from the paper chains and was offering it at August Brent +5 cents, with the best bid seen at August -5 cents.
"Any premium to August would be a bonus," said one dealer.
Some traders said the market had been kept artificially high last week by a French and a U.S. refiner trying to lift profits on swaps positions.

"In retrospect, some of the numbers we saw last week were a bit expensive...when you see cargoes being passed along the chains then it should mean the wet market is weaker than the 15-day market," said one trader.
But while Brent cargoes have been passed along the chains, none from the August loading programme have been left unclaimed at the five o'clock deadline, others noted.
The Brent paper market was quiet, although CFDs were talked weaker in reaction to Friday's fall on Dated Brent.
Non-Brent North Sea grades, especially Ekofisk and Forties were in good demand last week, keeping differentials firm.
Market speculation that there were renewed production or pipeline problems at the Forties system could not be immediately confirmed.

In the Mediterranean, Urals were still assessed around Dated Brent -60 cents with first decade August loading sold out. Traders heard that a large early August cargo had been resold on Friday at Dated Brent -57 cents.
"If you want prompt barrels then you have to pay up," said one trader.
A resumption of Iraqi sour crude exports is not expected before mid-August.
